nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{G}$ is the always operator.
nodes.title: Idempotence of always

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (always eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there are infinitely many $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Always eventually means infinitely often

nodes.summary:
For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ ("always $\varphi$") is defined as $
eg\,\mathbf{F}\,
eg\varphi$, the negation of "eventually $
eg\varphi$".
nodes.title: The always operator of LTL

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every atom $a$, the word $w$ satisfies the atomic formula $a$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w_0$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an atom

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters and every ω-word $w$, the word $w$ does not satisfy the LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) under $v$.
nodes.title: Falsity is never satisfied

nodes.summary: The LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) is defined as $\neg\top$, the negation of the truth constant $\top$.
nodes.title: Falsity in LTL

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ (eventually always $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there is $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge n$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Eventually always means from some point on

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Semantics of eventually

nodes.summary: For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ ("eventually $\varphi$") is defined as the until formula $\top \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \varphi$.
nodes.title: The eventually operator of LTL

nodes.summary: For a type $A$ of atoms, the formulas of linear temporal logic (LTL) over $A$ are generated inductively: every atom $a \in A$ is a formula, the truth constant $\top$ is a formula, and if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so are the negation $\neg\varphi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, the next formula $\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ and the until formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \psi$.
nodes.title: Formulas of linear temporal logic

nodes.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction $(\varphi \to \psi) \wedge (\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.
nodes.title: Bi-implication in LTL

nodes.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \vee \psi$.
nodes.title: Implication in LTL

nodes.summary: Given a valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, the ω-language of an LTL formula $\varphi$ is the set of ω-words that satisfy $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Language of an LTL formula

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ belongs to the ω-language of $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the language of a formula

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\neg\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{X}\,\neg\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.
nodes.title: Next is self-dual

nodes.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the disjunction $\varphi \vee \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \wedge 
eg\psi)$.
nodes.title: Disjunction in LTL

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and all LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\psi$ and it satisfies $\varphi$ or $\mathbf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi)$, all under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.
nodes.title: Expansion law for release

nodes.summary: For a valuation of atoms on letters, an ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) if and only if for every position $k$, either $\psi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ or $\varphi$ holds at some position $j < k$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Semantics of release

nodes.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the release formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{R}} \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} 
eg\psi)$, the dual of until.
nodes.title: The release operator of LTL

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $a$ an atom and $k$ a natural number. The atomic formula $a$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the letter $w(k)$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an atom at a position

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be an ω-word and, for a natural number $k$, let $w^{(k)}$ be its suffix starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. For every valuation of atoms on letters, every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every natural number $j$, $\varphi$ holds at position $j$ of $w^{(k)}$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at position $k + j$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction on a suffix

nodes.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ holds at position $0$ of $w$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction at position zero

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $k$ a natural number and $\varphi$ an LTL formula. Then $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ when the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$, satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction at a position

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters of an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $f \colon \Sigma' \to \Sigma$ be a map, and let $w$ be an ω-word over $\Sigma'$. For every LTL formula $\varphi$, the relabelled word $i \mapsto f(w(i))$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under the valuation that makes an atom $a$ true at a letter $s$ of $\Sigma'$ exactly when $v$ makes $a$ true at $f(s)$.
nodes.title: Relabelling the letters of an ω-word

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation that says which atoms are true at each letter, and for an ω-word $w$ and a natural number $k$ let $w^{(k)}$ be the suffix $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. Whether $w$ satisfies an LTL formula $\varphi$ under $v$, written $w \models \varphi$, is defined by recursion on $\varphi$: an atom $a$ holds when $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w(0)$; truth always holds; $\neg \varphi$ holds when $\varphi$…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of LTL formulas on ω-words

nodes.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ until $\psi$) if and only if either $w$ satisfies $\psi$, or $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ and also satisfies $\mathsf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi)$, that is, next ($\varphi$ until $\psi$).
nodes.title: Expansion law for until

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
